title: Skald bundle manifest, version 1
description: Defines version 1 of the bundle manifest. Released and immutable: changed meaning requires a new version, not an edit here. This exact document is served at two paths -- schemas/manifest/v1.schema.json, selected by a manifest's schema_version, and schemas/manifest.schema.json, the published path a consumer reads. dev/validate-manifests.sh asserts the two are identical and puts every fixture through BOTH, so the published path can never validate something the released version rejects. Structure only: this schema cannot express path containment, inventory membership or entrypoint resolution, which the semantic validator owns and which dev/fixtures/manifests/expectations.json labels as semantic.

schema_version.description: Exactly 1. A higher number is a newer format this validator must refuse rather than guess at.

type.description: A content type the registry recognises, mirroring content_type_known in V1__content_registry.sql. Being listed here is not a promise that a bundle of this type can be built: the recipe matrix decides that, and an unsupported one is refused with an explicit unsupported-type error rather than a schema violation.

runtime.description: The language and its exact version. No range, no 'latest', no download URL: the server picks a digest-pinned base from this, and a moving target cannot be pinned.

entrypoint.description: A path relative to app/, or '.' for the payload root. What it must denote depends on the language and is checked semantically: Python names a regular .py file present in files; R names a directory, validated through the files beneath it rather than by an entry of its own. This schema only constrains the string's shape.

dependencies.description: Always a regular file in files. format and the file it names are checked against the language by the semantic validator; a renv.lock declared under a Python runtime is a manifest disagreement, not a schema error.

files.description: Every regular payload file under app/, and nothing else. Directories are never members, which is why an R entrypoint is resolved through this list rather than found in it. manifest.json itself is excluded. The server verifies these hashes against the bytes it received; a publisher's hash is a declaration, not proof.

size.description: Bytes, as an integer. Bounds are operator policy and are enforced against the actual streamed bytes as well as this declaration.

executable.description: The only file mode a publisher may influence. Ownership, timestamps, setuid/setgid/sticky bits and extended attributes are stripped.

payloadPath.description: A relative, slash-separated path under app/. The pattern rejects an absolute path, a backslash and any control character; '.' and '..' segments, empty segments, NFC normalisation, case collisions and containment are the semantic validator's, because a regular expression cannot decide them.
